issue_paraphrase: The consistency checker on a receiving node rejects an index entry for a directory whose size field equals the fixed synthetic directory size value (a small nonzero constant) that other Syncthing versions stamp on directories during scanning. Such entries get flagged with 'non-file type with nonzero size', the directories are treated as invalid protocol data, and mixed-version synchronization of directory entries is disrupted. Size-zero directories and symlinks must also remain valid.
fix_summary: checkFileInfoConsistency (lib/protocol/protocol.go) now allows directories to carry either size 0 or the SyntheticDirectorySize constant; symlinks must carry size 0. Previously ANY non-file with nonzero size was rejected. Test case table TestCheckConsistency extended with directory/symlink size combinations.
notes: Pure function test, no network, sub-second at 1 CPU. SyntheticDirectorySize=128 already exists at the parent (introduced by 'stop treating dirs as having size 128'). The test is a table-driven case in TestCheckConsistency, so the author can point at 'directory entries with the synthetic size are rejected' without ever running a connection. lib/protocol is a heavy package to compile first time (~30-60s at 1 CPU with warm module cache), but the test itself is instant.

issue_paraphrase: Nodes running up-to-date Syncthing send block-data requests with a zero byte count (for empty files), but the receiving node treats any request size of zero as a protocol violation: the dispatcher terminates the connection with an error instead of replying. The two nodes then keep dropping the connection whenever such a request arrives, so an empty file transfer between a mixed-version pair fails to complete.
fix_summary: Two-part fix. lib/protocol/protocol.go: dispatcherLoop now rejects only strictly negative request sizes (msg.Size < 0), accepting the zero-sized requests current versions actually send; lib/model/folder_sendrecv.go: copierRoutine and pullerRoutine skip zero-size blocks as no-ops instead of running them through the limiter/request path, and TestPullCtxCancel uses Size:42 so it still exercises the cancellation path.
notes: Regression test uses the in-package in-memory connection harness (testutil.NewBlockingRW/NoopRW), no real sockets or network. Watch out: the branch condition is symmetric and easy to 'fix' wrongly (rejecting negatives only vs accepting zero) - TestRequestZeroSize requires the rawConnection to actually reply to a size-0 request. Golden test lives in lib/protocol/protocol_test.go which also contains TestRequestMaxSize (requires MaxRequestSize const, already present at the parent). lib/model changes are not exercised by the golden test; do not require lib/model tests as they are slower (~minutes to compile) and some need real folder setups.

issue_paraphrase: After an update tightened symlink handling so folder files are opened without following symlinks, ignore rules are no longer loaded when .stignore is itself a symbolic link to the real rules file (a common keep-your-dotfiles setup). Folder scans log an 'open .../.stignore: too many levels of symbolic links' failure and the configured ignore patterns are silently not applied, so files that should be excluded are scanned and synced.
fix_summary: Introduced a new OptFollow open flag in lib/fs (filesystem.go + basicfs_unix.go/basicfs_windows.go) that clears the default O_NOFOLLOW-style flag; lib/ignore/ignore.go's loadIgnoreFile now opens ignore files with fs.OptReadOnly|fs.OptFollow so a symlinked .stignore resolves to the real file. TestIgnoreThroughSymlink exercises loading via an actual symlink on a real temp-dir filesystem.
notes: Test uses a real (basic) filesystem in t.TempDir() and real symlinks - containers run as root, so symlink creation works. The test skips on Windows only. The fix spans the fs abstraction layer (flag plumbing) plus the ignore loader; a correct fix is not a one-line change - the author must add the opt flag through the filesystem interface. lib/ignore package compiles fast (~20-40s first time), test itself instant. No network.
